column1: # source: WRITTEN FROM KNOWLEDGE of standard historical phonology (Campbell, Historical Linguistics; Hock 1991; Blevins 2004, Evolutionary Phonology; Kümmel 2007). The Index Diachronica (https://chridd.nfshost.com/diachronica/, a hobbyist compilation) was used only as inspiration for coverage; nothing was copied from it.

# version: hand-authored 2026-11-03; revised 2026-11-04 (return paths: loss of aspiration and breathy voice, fortition, depalatalization; S030 and S165 conditioned; sinks round: S042 before stressed initial vowels, yod coalescence absorbs the j, S022 down, exits for ʔ, ɲ, j; hiatus round: S125-S127 and S205-S207 the hiatus family (fired as repairs, lect.resolve_hiatus), S126 written to parse, S175 staged; exits for the tap: S208 initial ɾ > r, S209 ɾ > l; revised 2026-11-07 (round 5, overused segments over all lects): S149 r > ɹ in the coda only, S173 Verner's law on f θ s x only (it also voiced h to ɦ), exits S210 ʁ > χ in the coda, S211 ʁ > h initially and between vowels, S212 ɫ > w, S213 ɦ > ∅ between vowels, S214 ʂ ʐ > s z; finish lane: exits for ɖ, S215 ɖ > ɽ between vowels, S216 ɽ > ɾ, S217 initial ɖ > r; sound lane 2026-11-08: S021, S091-S094 (long-distance, X* = any segments), S134 (ATR on height), S137, S142, S145, S162, S171 rewritten so they parse; S097 is the Tocharian-type merger of voiced and voiceless stops, weight 2 -> 1; chain rows staged (a > b > c is a > b then b > c), Grimm S177 and the Great Vowel Shift S179 one staged drag-order event each with S177 after sonorants too, S178 and S182 staged, S180 a plain raising of long mid vowels, S181 the shift's diphthongs opening)
# licence: original text for this repository; examples are textbook cases.

# rule notation: input > output / environment. V vowel, C consonant, N nasal, T voiceless stop, D voiced stop, # word boundary, _ the changing segment, [+stress]/[−stress] or V́ stressed vowel, Ṽ nasal vowel, ∅ zero, [αF] agreement in feature F, C* any number of consonants, {a, b} either context. Comma lists are parallel changes.

# cause: coarticulation | effort | perception | prosody | tonogenesis | dispersion | analogy (the dominant driver; judgement). articulators_or_axes_needed: lips, tongue_tip, tongue_blade, tongue_body, tongue_root, velum, larynx, pitch_ear (tone/pitch perception), timing (length, gemination), stress; 'none' for analogy. A people lacking an axis (e.g. no lips) should not get changes that need it.
# naturalness: 1 (rare, needs special conditions) .. 5 (extremely common, recurs independently everywhere). Judgement, loosely informed by Kümmel 2007 and Blevins 2004, not counted.

column7: Portuguese: Latin plēnum > Old Portuguese chẽo > cheio [ˈʃeju] 'full', cēna > cẽa > ceia 'supper', frēnum > freo > freio 'brake'

column3: ɾ > r / #_ (a word-initial tap becomes a trill)
column7: Spanish and Portuguese: the only rhotic allowed word-initially is the trill, so Latin rosa > Spanish rosa [ˈrosa]; Catalan likewise (roda [ˈrɔðə]); Albanian

column3: ɾ > l (the tap merges with l)
column7: Polynesian: Proto-Polynesian *r merged with *l in Hawaiian (PPn *rua 'two' > Hawaiian lua) and in Tongan loss chains; Proto-Bantu *d > l ~ ɾ in many daughters; Japanese loans show the same r ~ l perception

column3: ʁ > χ / _C, _# (the uvular r devoiced in the coda)
column7: Standard German Ort [ɔχt], Wort; Brazilian Portuguese (carioca) porta [ˈpɔχta]; then χ > h (S026)

column3: ʁ > h / #_, V_V (a uvular r weakened to h at the start of a word and between vowels)
column7: Brazilian Portuguese (Rio de Janeiro, Belo Horizonte): rato [ˈhatu], rua [ˈhuɐ], carro [ˈkahu], after trilled r > ʁ ~ χ
Polish ł: Old Polish [ɫ] > modern [w] in all positions (łapa [ˈwapa], mały [ˈmawɨ]); Brazilian Portuguese coda l > w (Brasil [bɾaˈziw])

column3: ɦ > ∅ / V_V (breathy h lost between vowels)
column7: Hindi kahnā [kɛːnaː], rahnā [rɛːnaː] (intervocalic ɦ lost, the vowels fused); Gujarati, Bengali colloquial h-loss

column3: ʂ, ʐ > s, z (retroflex sibilants merge with the dental ones)
column7: Prakrit and Pali: Sanskrit viṣa > Pali visa 'poison', śiṣya > sissa; Mandarin zh ch sh [ʈʂ ʂ] as [ts s] in southern Mandarin and Taiwan

column3: ɖ > ɽ / V_V (the retroflex stop flapped between vowels)
column7: Hindi-Urdu: Middle Indo-Aryan ḍ between vowels is the flap ṛ, Prakrit ghoḍa > ghoṛā [ɡʱoːɽaː] 'horse', baḍa > baṛā 'big'; Vedic ḍ > ḷ between vowels (īḍe ~ īḷe)

column3: ɽ > ɾ (the retroflex flap merges with the tap)
column7: Eastern Bengali (Dhaka, Sylheti): ড় [ɽ] falls together with র [ɾ ~ r], so baṛi 'house' is said bari

column3: ɖ > r / #_ (a word-initial retroflex stop became r)
column7: Romani: Middle Indo-Aryan ḍomba > rom 'man, husband; Rom' (Matras 2002, Romani: A Linguistic Introduction)
